name: disorders of growth overview
title: Disorders of growth pathway: short stature splits first on growth velocity, then on whether weight fell before height; normal velocity means familial short stature or constitutional delay (bone age on time vs delayed); weight falling first means chronic illness, undernutrition or an intrauterine cause; a short, relatively chubby child points to growth hormone deficiency or hypothyroidism; genetic causes include Turner syndrome and skeletal dysplasia; each column gives causes and clues, investigations, and treatment or outcome, with panels on measuring, evaluating growth, when to worry, the work-up, other endocrine causes and other genetic syndromes

nodes.title: Short stature: is growth velocity normal, and did the WEIGHT fall before the HEIGHT?
lines: short stature = height 2 standard deviations (SD) or more below the mean (< 3rd percentile)
chronic illness: weight falls FIRST · endocrine: short and relatively CHUBBY for height

nodes.title: NORMAL growth velocity: normal variants
lines: the MOST COMMON causes of short stature
no systemic or endocrine disease

nodes.title: LOW velocity · WEIGHT falls FIRST
lines: weight loss or no weight gain PRECEDES the height drop
~more gradual drop-off

nodes.title: LOW velocity · short and relatively CHUBBY: ENDOCRINE
lines: weight > height · usually ACUTE growth failure
uncommon · consider in ANY child with markedly reduced height velocity

nodes.title: LOW velocity · GENETIC
lines: look for dysmorphism, bone deformities and proportion
~Turner: always karyotype a short girl

nodes.title: Familial short stature (FSS)
lines: NORMAL variant
parental target is LOW

nodes.title: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP)
lines: NORMAL variant · running LATE

nodes.title: Chronic illness, undernutrition, intrauterine
lines: GENERAL PAEDIATRIC causes
weight falls before height

nodes.title: Growth hormone (GH) deficiency
lines: MOST COMMON endocrine cause
1 in 3500–4000 children

nodes.title: Hypothyroidism
lines: slow growth WITH weight gain
thyroid hormone also drives childhood growth

nodes.title: Turner syndrome
lines: all or part of an X MISSING
1 in 2000–2500 newborn girls

nodes.title: Skeletal dysplasia
lines: GENETIC bone disorder
DISPROPORTIONATE short stature

nodes.title: Height at or below 3rd percentile
lines: growth rate low-normal

nodes.title: Puberty ON TIME
lines: pubertal growth spurt at the normal age

nodes.title: Short parents
lines: mid-parental height is low

nodes.title: Height AND weight at or below 3rd percentile
lines: growth velocity low-normal

nodes.title: POSITIVE family history
lines: ask about delayed puberty in the parents

nodes.title: Small for gestational age (SGA)
lines: maternal infection, smoking, alcohol, systemic illness · fetal malnutrition, placental insufficiency
most catch up by 2 yr · 10% do NOT: pathologic

nodes.title: Poor intake
lines: isolated undernutrition: cleft palate, psychosocial deprivation, eating disorders

nodes.title: Malabsorption
lines: celiac, Crohn's, liver or pancreas, lactose intolerance

nodes.title: Other chronic illness
lines: chronic renal failure · rheumatologic · cyanotic congenital heart disease, cystic fibrosis, asthma · malignancy · immunologic

nodes.title: NORMAL birth weight + length
lines: then severe post-natal growth restriction
neonatal HYPOGLYCAEMIA · prolonged JAUNDICE

nodes.title: Face + body
lines: poor nasal bridge, frontal bossing · midline defects: high or cleft palate
late, irregular teeth · late anterior fontanelle · thin hair, poor nails · high voice

nodes.title: MICROPENIS
lines: esp. if gonado-tropins also low

nodes.title: Mechanism
lines: GH-releasing hormone (GHRH) or pituitary fails

nodes.title: Congenital
lines: ectopic or hypoplastic pituitary · midline defects, other pituitary hormones low

nodes.title: Acquired
lines: sellar tumours (craniopharyngioma) · cranial irradiation · head injury

nodes.title: Case: 12-year-old girl
lines: linear growth slows, weight speeds up
dry skin · fatigue · hair loss, brittle hair + nails

nodes.title: Signs
lines: puffy features · GOITRE · cold intolerance · constipation

nodes.title: SHORT STATURE in 95–100%
lines: the MOST COMMON feature
normal GH but bone resists it, or GH deficiency + bone resistance

nodes.title: Dysmorphic
lines: webbed neck · short 4th metacarpals · cubitus valgus (↑ carrying angle) · hypoplastic nails · lymphedema of hands + feet

nodes.title: Hypogonadism
lines: streak ovaries 90% · thelarche 10–15% · menarche 1% (mosaic) · pubarche 100% (adrenals normal) · infertility > 99%

nodes.title: Associated
lines: congenital heart disease (coarctation) · renal (horseshoe kidney) · thyroid, type 1 diabetes, celiac · metabolic syndrome, type 2 diabetes · hearing · learning: non-verbal, arithmetic, visuospatial · ↑ attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder

nodes.title: By age
lines: neonate: dysmorphism, heart, kidney · child: short, hypothyroid · teen: absent puberty, primary amenorrhea

nodes.title: Achondroplasia, hypochondroplasia
lines: the MOST COMMON
fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene

nodes.title: Osteogenesis imperfecta
lines: fragile bones that fracture easily · BLUE SCLERAE, easy bruising, deafness
dominant type 1 collagen: COL1A1 or COL1A2

nodes.title: Bone age = chronological age
lines: ~normal bone age is ± 1 yr

nodes.title: Mid-parental height
lines: genetic potential: LOW

nodes.title: Bone age DELAYED
lines: closer to the height-age than to the real age

nodes.title: FIRST rule out chronic illness
lines: complete blood count (CBC), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR)
renal: creatinine, blood urea nitrogen (BUN), electrolytes, albumin, calcium, phosphate
tissue transglutaminase antibodies: celiac screen

nodes.title: History
lines: neonatal: SGA? · systems: chronic illness?

nodes.title: Random GH is of NO VALUE
lines: GH is released in PULSES

nodes.title: 1 · Screen: IGF-1 / IGFBP-3
lines: serum insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1) and IGF binding protein 3

nodes.title: 2 · TWO provocative STIMULATION tests
lines: arginine · clonidine · glucagon · insulin tolerance test (adults: provokes hypoglycaemia)
deficient: GH response < 8 µg/L

nodes.title: Diagnostic criteria
lines: height < 3rd percentile · velocity < 25th percentile · bone age > 2 SD delayed · 2 failed tests

nodes.title: Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH)
lines: case: 467 mU/L (normal 0.35–5.55)
in EVERY initial work-up

nodes.title: KARYOTYPE every short girl
lines: 45,X 60% · 45,X mosaic with a normal line 15%
structural X (deletion, isochromosome, ring) 10% · other 15%

nodes.title: Exam: proportion + bone deformities
lines: ~skeletal survey, genetic testing †

nodes.title: Reassurance †
lines: ~normal adult height †

nodes.title: Treat the cause †
lines: nutrition · gluten-free diet for celiac †

nodes.title: Recombinant GH
lines: subcutaneous injection 6–7× a week until growth is complete

nodes.title: Dose by WEIGHT and INDICATION
lines: GH deficiency ≠ Turner dose · US$10,000–30,000 a year

nodes.title: Untreated
lines: ~2 brothers: 5 ft 11 in vs 4 ft 7 in

nodes.title: GH from first growth failure
lines: often 4–6 yr · 0.35–0.375 mg/kg/week
+5–7 cm over 8 yr · parents' height matters

nodes.title: ESTROGEN replacement
lines: most will NOT enter puberty on their own

nodes.title: Final height
lines: mean 144 cm (132–154) · ~20 cm below background

nodes.title: Supportive †
lines: ~limb lengthening in selected cases †

panels.title: Measure and plot
items: under 2 yr: LENGTH, World Health Organization (WHO) charts · head firm on the board, knees straight, foot at a right angle
2–20 yr: HEIGHT, Centers for Disease Control (CDC) charts · Frankfurt plane, barefoot, knees straight, heels on the board
age- and sex-specific chart · velocity from measurements 1 yr apart

panels.title: Evaluate growth: 4 questions
items: GENETIC POTENTIAL: mid-parental height = (mother + father + 13 cm) ÷ 2 for boys, − 13 cm for girls · e.g. 160 + 185 → 166 cm
HEIGHT-AGE: the age at which this height is the 50th percentile · shorter child, younger height-age
GROWTH VELOCITY: measurements 1 yr apart
GROWTH POTENTIAL: bone age, single X-ray of the LEFT wrist · normal ± 1 yr · delayed or advanced: NOT ALWAYS a problem

panels.title: When to worry
items: velocity < 4.5 cm/yr from age 4 to puberty
crossing percentiles after 18 months and before puberty
> 2 SD below mid-parental height
height < 3rd percentile
~normal: infancy fastest (nutrition, thyroid, bone) · childhood GH-driven + thyroid · puberty: sex steroids + bigger, more frequent GH pulses · average 5–6 cm/yr

panels.title: Work-up of a short child
items: HISTORY: growth, development · neonatal: SGA, hypoglycaemia, jaundice · parents' heights, delayed puberty · chronic illness · endocrine
EXAM: accurate height, weight, growth curve · puberty · chronic illness · GH deficiency, goitre, Cushing signs · dysmorphism (Turner) · bone deformities · midline defects
FIRST: CBC, ESR, renal panel, celiac antibodies, TSH, hand X-ray for bone age
THEN consider: karyotype (ALWAYS a short girl) · IGF-1 · provocative GH test

panels.title: Other endocrine + bone causes
items: GLUCOCORTICOID EXCESS: growth slows + weight gain · central obesity, buffalo hump, striae, hirsutism, acne · steroid therapy, Cushing syndrome (rare in children)
RICKETS: hypophosphatemic (poor growth, bowed legs) · vitamin D deficiency
PSEUDOHYPOPARATHYROIDISM: resistance to parathyroid hormone · short + obese, round face, developmental delay · short metacarpals: knuckle-knuckle-dimple-dimple (Archibald's sign)

panels.title: Other genetic syndromes
items: Down syndrome (trisomy 21)
PRADER-WILLI: chromosome 15 microdeletion · hypotonia, feeding difficulty, developmental delay · failure to thrive, then hyperphagia + severe obesity
NOONAN: short · congenital heart disease (pulmonary stenosis) · delayed speech or motor milestones
SILVER-RUSSELL: severe intrauterine + postnatal growth retardation · triangular face, prominent forehead
SHOX gene (on the X): short forearms + lower legs, Madelung deformity
